stem: An AI invoice-processing tool cost $400,000 to deploy and $100,000 a year to run. It saves 12,000 staff hours a year at a loaded cost of $50 per hour. Which statement about the first-year return is accurate?

choices.text: Annual savings are $120,000, so the tool will not break even for more than four years under current assumptions
The tool loses money in year one because staff hours saved cannot be converted into dollars for a business case
Annual savings are $600,000, so the first year returns $500,000 net because deployment is a one-time cost
Annual savings are $600,000, so the first year returns about $100,000 net after deployment and running costs

stem: A mid-sized insurer wants AI-assisted claims triage within six months. It has strong claims data, two ML engineers, and no plan to sell AI products. Which sourcing approach best fits?

choices.text: Delay the initiative until the insurer can hire a research team of twenty scientists for custom development
Buy a closed third-party product that cannot use the insurer's own data, to avoid any integration work
Build on managed AWS AI services using its own claims data, rather than developing models from scratch
Develop a proprietary foundation model from scratch so the insurer fully owns every layer of the technology

stem: Two competitors deploy the same public foundation model for customer service. One consistently outperforms the other in customer satisfaction. Which factor most likely explains the difference?

choices.text: The better-performing company runs the model in a different AWS Region that has newer data centers and hardware
The better-performing company renamed the assistant with a friendlier brand name that customers remember more easily
The better-performing company pays a higher per-token price for the same model, which improves its answer quality
Integration with its own customer history, product data, and support workflows that the other company lacks

stem: A retail COO wants 'an AI strategy' after a competitor announced a chatbot. What should come first when shaping the strategy?

choices.text: Hire a chief AI officer and wait for that person to decide which departments should use AI at all
Launch a chatbot within 30 days so the company matches the competitor's announcement as quickly as possible
Identify the business outcomes the company most needs to improve and where AI could plausibly help
Select the most capable foundation model on the market and license it before defining any use cases

stem: A marketing team reports that its AI content tool 'generated 4,000 articles this quarter.' The CFO is unimpressed. Which metric would better show business value?

choices.text: The number of employees who logged in to the tool at least once during the quarter under review
The number of prompts marketers wrote each week while using the tool to generate the articles
The average word count of generated articles compared with the articles the team wrote by hand last year
Change in qualified leads or conversions attributed to the content compared with the prior baseline

stem: A hospital network is choosing its first generative AI initiative. Option 1 summarizes internal meeting notes. Option 2 drafts patient discharge instructions sent directly to patients. Both have similar projected value. Which reasoning best guides the first choice?

choices.text: Start with meeting summaries, which carry lower risk and let the organization build skills and governance first
Start with discharge instructions, because patient-facing use cases always produce the fastest return on investment
Start with neither until regulators publish rules specific to generative AI in every jurisdiction the network serves
Start with both at once, because running two pilots in parallel always halves the time to enterprise adoption

stem: A company wants to judge whether its AI sales assistant, not a seasonal upturn, caused a 9% rise in win rates. Which evaluation design gives the most credible answer?

choices.text: Count how many proposals the assistant drafted, and assume each drafted proposal produced one additional win
Compare a group of sales reps using the assistant with a similar group not using it over the same period
Ask the sales reps using the assistant whether they believe it helped them close more deals this quarter
Compare this quarter's win rate with the same quarter five years ago, before any AI tools were in use

stem: A company worries about lock-in to one foundation model provider as models improve quickly. Which approach best preserves flexibility without slowing delivery?

choices.text: Build applications against a platform that offers several models through a common API, and keep prompts and evaluations portable
Sign a five-year exclusive contract with the current leading provider in exchange for a volume discount
Build every application on a different model provider so that no single provider ever handles more than one workload at a time
Avoid foundation models entirely until the market consolidates around a single long-term technology leader

stem: A logistics firm's AI pilot met its technical goals, but executives disagree on whether to scale it. Which artifact would best support a go or no-go decision?

choices.text: A detailed architecture diagram showing every AWS service the pilot used during its three months of testing
A press release draft announcing the pilot's success to customers and investors ahead of the final decision
A business case comparing measured pilot results with the costs, risks, and resources required to scale
A list of all the prompts and model settings the team experimented with while tuning the pilot's outputs

stem: A company is choosing KPIs for an AI document-review tool used by its legal team. Which pair combines an efficiency measure with a quality measure?

choices.text: Number of pages processed per week and the average page count of contracts reviewed by the tool
Monthly model inference cost and the number of different model versions tested during the quarter
Number of contracts uploaded to the tool and the number of lawyers with active user accounts
Review time per contract and the rate of issues missed that were later found by senior lawyers

stem: A software vendor considers partnering with a specialized AI firm instead of building a capability in-house. When is a partnership the strongest choice?

choices.text: When the vendor wants to avoid defining any requirements and prefers the partner to decide the business goals
When the capability is needed soon, is not a core differentiator, and the partner has proven expertise the vendor lacks
When the capability is the vendor's main source of competitive advantage and must remain entirely proprietary
When the vendor already has a large, experienced in-house team that has built and operated the same capability successfully before

stem: A manufacturer's AI steering committee wants a balanced portfolio of AI initiatives. Which TWO practices support that goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Choose initiatives mainly by which AI techniques are newest, to keep the company's reputation for innovation
Review each initiative regularly and pause or stop those that miss agreed milestones
Approve only initiatives that require no new data collection, so work can start the week they are approved
Fund every proposal equally so that no department feels its ideas were treated unfairly by the committee
Mix quick, low-risk wins with a smaller number of longer-term initiatives that could create larger advantages

stem: A company's AI assistant cut average call time by 20%, but the CFO sees no reduction in cost. Which TWO follow-up questions best explain whether value is being realized? (Select TWO)

choices.text: How many tokens did the assistant use per call compared with the vendor's advertised average usage?
Which foundation model version was used, and has the vendor released a newer version since launch?
Did customer satisfaction or first-contact resolution change, since faster calls might hurt or help quality?
How many employees attended the assistant's launch training session and completed the online course?
Was the freed agent time redirected to other work, or did staffing and workload plans stay unchanged?

stem: A bank evaluates an AI solution from AWS Marketplace. Which TWO considerations matter most before committing? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Whether the vendor's marketing materials use the same terminology as the bank's internal documents
The number of other products the vendor lists on AWS Marketplace across unrelated industries
The color scheme of the vendor's user interface compared with the bank's corporate brand colors
The contract terms for data use, exit, and portability if the bank later changes providers
Whether the solution can work with the bank's data under its security and compliance requirements

stem: Finance asks whether to report an AI project's value as 'hours saved' or 'dollars saved.' The saved hours are being reassigned to new customer outreach rather than reducing headcount. Which reporting approach is most accurate?

choices.text: Report hours redeployed and the outcomes of the new outreach, rather than claiming a direct cost reduction
Report the vendor's advertised savings figure, since it was calculated from many customers' deployments
Report nothing until headcount is reduced, since value only counts when salaries are removed from the budget
Report the full dollar value of the saved hours as a cost reduction, even though payroll costs did not change

stem: A company's AI roadmap lists initiatives but no owners, timelines, or success measures. What is the most important improvement to make the roadmap actionable?

choices.text: Assign an accountable business owner, a timeline, and measurable success criteria to each initiative
Remove all timelines so teams can experiment freely without pressure to show results by a certain date
Add more initiatives to the roadmap so that every department has at least one AI project assigned to it
Replace the roadmap with a list of AI vendors the company has already met during the past year

stem: A fashion retailer has 15 years of detailed customer style preferences and returns data. How can this asset create a durable competitive advantage with generative AI?

choices.text: Delete older data because generative AI models only need the most recent few months of customer information
Use the proprietary data to personalize recommendations and content in ways competitors using public data cannot copy
Sell the raw customer data to competitors so the whole industry benefits from better generative AI models
Publish the data openly so foundation model providers include it in their next public model training runs

stem: A company's AI chatbot deflected 40% of support contacts, yet support costs rose. Investigation shows customers often call after unhelpful chatbot answers. What does this reveal about the chosen KPI?

choices.text: Support costs cannot be linked to chatbot performance, so no KPI can ever capture the chatbot's real business value
The chatbot should deflect even more contacts, since higher deflection always lowers total support costs
Deflection rate is the correct KPI, and the cost increase must be caused by unrelated seasonal factors
Deflection rate alone ignored resolution, so failed conversations created repeat contacts that raised costs

stem: A lender's AI credit model approves applicants from one postal region at a much lower rate than others with similar finances. The model does not use region as an input. What is the most likely cause, and the right first step?

choices.text: The gap proves the training data was stolen or tampered with, so the model should be retired and the incident reported to police
The model is working as intended, since lenders are allowed to use any statistically predictive pattern
Other inputs act as proxies for region, so the team should measure outcomes by group and investigate those features
The model cannot be biased because region is not an input, so the approval gap must be a reporting error

stem: A company tells customers when they are chatting with an AI assistant and explains what data the assistant uses. Which responsible AI principle does this primarily support?

choices.text: Robustness, so the assistant keeps working correctly when inputs are unusual or noisy
Veracity, so every answer the assistant gives is guaranteed to be factually correct
Transparency, so users understand when AI is involved and how it reaches its outputs
Controllability, so administrators can shut the assistant down during an emergency

stem: A European retailer plans an AI system that screens job applicants. Which governance step should happen before deployment?

choices.text: A decision to keep the system's use secret from applicants so that candidates cannot game the screening
A documented risk assessment covering fairness, human oversight, and applicable regulations for high-impact uses
A contract clause stating that the software vendor alone is legally responsible for any unfair outcomes
A marketing plan announcing that hiring decisions will soon be fully automated, to attract more applicants to open roles

stem: A company has 30 teams experimenting with generative AI and no common rules. Leadership wants consistency without stopping innovation. Which governance structure fits best?

choices.text: A rule that only the IT department may use generative AI, with every other team required to submit tickets for each request
A complete ban on generative AI until an external auditor certifies every possible future use case
No central policy, so each team can decide its own rules according to the needs of its own customers
A cross-functional AI governance group that sets shared policies and risk tiers while teams build within them

stem: Employees are pasting confidential customer contracts into a free public chatbot to summarize them. Which response best reduces the risk while meeting the business need?

choices.text: Provide an approved AI tool with data protections for this task and set a clear policy on public tools
Discipline the employees involved and take no further action, since the acceptable-use policy already existed
Allow public chatbots to continue, since summaries do not contain the original contract text
Block all internet access for employees who work with customer contracts until further notice

stem: A board asks which risk is specific to generative AI compared with traditional predictive models. Which answer is best?

choices.text: Performing worse over time if the business environment changes after the system is deployed
Producing fluent but fabricated content, such as invented citations or facts presented as true
Requiring computing resources and ongoing operating costs to run the system in production
Needing large amounts of historical data to learn patterns before the system can make any useful predictions

stem: An insurer can choose a slightly more accurate model that cannot explain its decisions or a slightly less accurate model whose reasons are clear. Customers can appeal claim denials. Which choice is most defensible?

choices.text: The more accurate model, because accuracy always outweighs every other consideration in insurance
The more accurate model, with explanations written afterward by staff who guess the model's reasoning
Neither model, because any automated support for claims decisions is inherently irresponsible
The explainable model, because appeals require clear reasons and the accuracy difference is small

stem: An auditor asks a company for documentation describing each production model's intended use, limitations, training data sources, and evaluation results. Which artifact is designed for this?

choices.text: A model card that records purpose, data, performance, and known limitations for each model
An architecture diagram showing the network paths between the model and the application servers
A cost report listing each model's monthly inference spending and the budget owner responsible
A release note announcing new features to customers each time the model is updated or retrained

stem: A bank's customer chatbot must never give investment advice and must hide account numbers in its replies. Which control addresses both requirements consistently?

Training every customer service agent to correct the chatbot when they notice a problem in chats
Guardrails that deny the investment advice topic and mask sensitive information in responses
A weekly manual review of a random sample of conversations to catch violations after they happen

Physically securing the data centers where the foundation models are hosted by AWS

Patching the underlying servers and hypervisors that run the managed Bedrock service

stem: A company deploys an AI tool that recommends which employees receive promotions. Which TWO practices best support fairness and accountability? (Select TWO)

Monitor recommendation outcomes across demographic groups and investigate unexplained gaps

stem: Six months after launch, a fraud model's alerts have become less accurate. Transaction patterns shifted after a new payment method was introduced. Which governance practice would have caught this sooner?

A policy requiring the model to be replaced every month regardless of how well it is performing
An annual report of how many fraud alerts the model generated compared with the previous year
Ongoing monitoring of model performance and input data against agreed thresholds, with alerts to owners

stem: A process owner says a new AI claims workflow will be 'human-in-the-loop.' What does this mean for how the process runs?

choices.text: A person writes every output by hand while the AI system watches and records the work
A person answers customer calls while the AI system listens for training data collection
A person reviews or approves AI outputs at defined points before action is taken
A person physically operates the computer hardware that runs the AI model at all times

stem: A company must decide who approves a new customer-facing AI use case. Which approach reflects good governance?

choices.text: The engineer who builds the system approves it alone, since they understand it better than anyone else in the company
A defined approval path that includes business, legal, security, and risk perspectives based on risk tier
Any employee can approve it, since AI use cases should never be slowed down by governance
The vendor approves it, since the vendor built the underlying foundation model being used

stem: A company's AI model uses customer data collected for billing to predict churn. What governance question arises first?

choices.text: Whether the churn model's dashboard will be ready for the next quarterly business review meeting
Whether the model should be retrained daily or weekly to keep the predictions current
Whether the billing team would like to receive a copy of the churn predictions each month
Whether using the data for this new purpose is permitted under consent and privacy obligations

stem: Which role is most important to name for each production AI system?

choices.text: An accountable business owner responsible for its outcomes and ongoing oversight
A travel coordinator responsible for booking trips for the model's developers
A designer responsible for choosing the colors and fonts of the system's user interface
A facilities manager responsible for the office where the model's team sits

stem: A company's AI assistant might give outdated policy answers after policies change. Which control reduces this risk?

choices.text: Increase the assistant's temperature so that answers vary and users double-check them
Train employees to ignore the assistant whenever a policy question seems important
Add a footnote telling users that policies may have changed since the assistant was trained
Keep the assistant's source documents current and re-index them whenever policies change

stem: A company deploys AI to draft responses to regulator inquiries. Which safeguard is essential?

choices.text: Automatic sending of drafts to regulators to reduce the company's response time
Expert review and approval of every draft before it is sent to the regulator
Using the most creative model settings so responses sound more persuasive
Deleting drafts after sending so there is no record of AI involvement

stem: Which risk is most associated with AI systems trained on data scraped from the internet?

choices.text: Running more slowly than systems trained only on internal company data
Being unable to answer any question written in a language other than English
Inheriting inaccurate, biased, or copyrighted content from the source data
Requiring more electricity to display results on employees' laptop screens

stem: A company can improve its recommendation model by collecting more detailed personal data from users. Which approach best balances value and responsibility?

choices.text: Collect only data needed for clear benefit, with user consent and transparency about its use
Collect personal data without telling users, since disclosure might reduce sign-ups
Never use any personal data at all, even with consent, for any recommendation purpose
Collect as much personal data as possible, since more data always makes recommendation models better

stem: Which TWO practices help a company show that its AI governance is effective, not just documented? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A longer governance policy document with more detailed legal language
A company-wide email announcing that governance is now in place
Periodic internal audits that test whether controls are actually followed
A larger governance committee with more members from each department
Metrics on incidents, reviews completed, and issues resolved over time

stem: Which TWO controls best reduce the risk of employees over-trusting AI outputs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Present AI outputs as final decisions that employees cannot question
Hide the AI system's known error rates from the employees who use it
Remove any mention that outputs were generated by AI from the interface
Show confidence indicators or sources alongside AI outputs
Train employees on the system's limitations and when to verify outputs

stem: A company uses AI to summarize customer complaints for executives. Which risk to fairness should be checked?

choices.text: Whether the summaries are delivered on Monday morning or on Friday afternoon
Whether complaints from some customer groups are systematically underrepresented in summaries
Whether executives read the summaries on their phones or on their laptops
Whether the summaries use the company's preferred font and color scheme

stem: A company is creating an AI incident response process after a chatbot gave harmful advice. What is the main purpose of this process?

choices.text: To detect, contain, investigate, and learn from AI failures or harms quickly
To celebrate AI project launches with a company-wide internal communications plan
To negotiate AI vendor contracts before each renewal date arrives
To schedule regular upgrades of the office computers used by AI teams

stem: A chatbot vendor updates its model without notice, and the company's chatbot starts answering differently. Which practice would have caught this sooner?

choices.text: Automated regression tests on key questions that run regularly against the live system
Waiting for customers to complain on social media before investigating any behavior changes
Asking employees to guess whether the chatbot seems different from last month
Reading the vendor's annual report once a year to learn about product updates

stem: A company's AI model is highly accurate but uses a feature that is a close proxy for a protected characteristic. What should governance require?

choices.text: Add more proxy features so that no single feature has a large effect on the predictions
Assess whether using the feature causes unfair outcomes, and remove or mitigate it if it does
Keep the feature, since high accuracy justifies any feature the model happens to find useful for prediction
Hide the feature's name in documentation so that reviewers do not ask questions about it

stem: A company rates itself 'advanced' in AI maturity because it has run 30 pilots. None are in production. How should this be assessed?

choices.text: Maturity cannot be assessed until the company runs at least one hundred pilots
Maturity is advanced, since the number of pilots run is the main indicator of an organization's AI maturity
Maturity is closer to early stage, since operating AI in production with measurable value is missing
Maturity is irrelevant, since only the number of AI tools purchased matters

stem: A readiness review finds the company has good data but no process to decide which AI projects get funded. Which gap is this?

choices.text: A data quality gap that prevents models from producing accurate predictions
A talent gap that prevents the company from hiring enough data scientists
An infrastructure gap that prevents the company from running its models reliably at scale
A governance and portfolio management gap that prevents prioritized investment

stem: A company's AI models need data that currently takes three weeks to extract from legacy systems. What foundational improvement helps most?

choices.text: Asking data scientists to type the legacy data manually into shared spreadsheets each week
Automated, reliable data pipelines that deliver the needed data on a regular schedule
Waiting for the legacy systems to be retired before starting any AI work at all
Buying more laptops for the data science team so they can extract data faster

stem: A company plans generative AI across departments and wants consistent security and cost control. Which foundation fits best?

choices.text: A single shared password for all employees to access every model the company has approved
Separate accounts with each team choosing any model provider it likes and managing its own security settings
A shared, governed access layer to approved models with central logging, guardrails, and cost tracking
No central controls, so that each team can move as fast as possible without any coordination

stem: Employees ask whether AI will change how their performance is evaluated. Which leadership response builds trust?

choices.text: Announce that performance will be measured only by how often each person uses the AI tools
Avoid the question until the rollout is fully complete, so that employees stay focused on their current work
Tell employees that nothing will ever change, even though roles are expected to change
Explain openly how roles and evaluation will change, and involve employees in defining new expectations

stem: A company wants to build a culture of responsible experimentation with AI. Which practice supports this best?

choices.text: Encourage small, safe experiments with clear guardrails and share lessons from both successes and failures
Punish teams whose AI experiments fail, so that only guaranteed successes are ever attempted by the company
Allow unlimited experimentation with production customer data and no review of any kind
Restrict experimentation to a single executive who decides what everyone else may try

stem: Which leadership behavior most accelerates AI adoption across a company?

choices.text: Leaders delegating all AI discussion to IT and avoiding the topic personally
Leaders announcing AI goals once and not referring to them again afterward
Leaders asking teams to adopt AI while exempting themselves from using it
Leaders visibly using AI tools themselves and sharing how they apply them

stem: A company has scaled an AI tool, and requests for new features are piling up from every department. Which approach manages this best?

choices.text: Build every requested feature immediately so that no department ever feels ignored by the product team
A product-style backlog prioritized by value, with a clear owner making trade-off decisions
Let the loudest department decide which features are built each quarter
Stop accepting feature requests so the team can focus on maintenance only

stem: A multinational wants to roll out an AI assistant in countries with different languages and regulations. Which approach reduces risk?

choices.text: Adapt and validate the assistant for each market's language and rules before launching there
Let each country build its own assistant from scratch without sharing any components
Launch the same configuration everywhere at once, since AI works exactly the same way in every country
Launch only in the headquarters country and forbid other offices from ever using it

stem: After scaling an AI tool, usage drops in several teams after three months. What should leaders do first?

choices.text: Replace the tool with the newest product available on the market immediately
Mandate daily usage for every employee and monitor compliance each week
Talk to users to understand why usage fell and fix the causes they identify
Assume the tool is no longer needed and shut it down across the company

stem: Which TWO questions assess whether a company's culture is ready for AI? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Has the company chosen a mascot for its AI transformation program yet?
Does the company use the latest version of its office productivity software?
Does every employee have a personal parking space at the headquarters office?
Are teams comfortable experimenting and learning from failed attempts?
Do leaders make decisions using data and evidence rather than instinct alone?

stem: Which TWO data foundations most enable a company to scale AI use cases? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A catalog that makes trusted datasets easy to find and understand
Keeping all data on individual laptops for faster local access by analysts
Manual data exports emailed between teams on request
Separate copies of the same dataset maintained by every team
Consistent data quality checks built into the pipelines

stem: A company's AI program is led entirely by IT, and business units see it as 'IT's project.' Which change best improves ownership?

choices.text: Stop reporting AI results to business units so they are not distracted
Rename the program so it sounds less technical to business leaders
Make business leaders co-own AI initiatives and accountable for their outcomes
Give IT sole control of all AI decisions to avoid any confusion about ownership

stem: Which TWO practices help sustain AI value after enterprise rollout? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Removing the feedback channel so users focus on using the tool as delivered
Ongoing measurement of outcomes against targets with regular reviews
Disbanding the project team immediately once the rollout is announced
Stopping all monitoring once the system has run for one month successfully
A funded team responsible for maintenance, updates, and user support

stem: A company debates whether to wait for perfect data before starting AI or to start with imperfect data. Which approach is most practical?

choices.text: Buy third-party data to replace all internal data, regardless of relevance or cost
Start where data is good enough for the use case, and improve data quality as value is proven
Wait until all company data is perfectly clean before starting any AI use case at all
Ignore data quality entirely, since modern AI models fix any data problems automatically

stem: A company's model predicts equipment failures but only after the failure has begun. Operations want earlier warnings. What change to the model's design is needed?

choices.text: Reduce the amount of sensor data used so the model runs faster on each reading
Change the color of the alert messages so operators notice them more quickly
Increase the number of employees who read the model's alerts after each failure has already begun
Train it to predict failures a set time ahead, using data from before past failures started

stem: A museum wants visitors to ask spoken questions about exhibits and hear spoken answers. Which combination of capabilities fits?

choices.text: Fraud detection, document extraction, and translation of exhibit labels into codes
Image generation, sentiment analysis, and demand forecasting for exhibit visitor numbers
Speech-to-text, a question-answering model grounded in exhibit information, and text-to-speech
Recommendation systems alone, since they can hear and answer spoken questions directly

stem: A company wants a model to follow its brand voice across thousands of product descriptions. Prompts alone give inconsistent results. What is the logical next step?

choices.text: Fine-tune a model on examples of approved brand-voice descriptions
Switch to a speech model that reads descriptions aloud in a brand voice
Remove the brand guidelines from the prompt to simplify the request
Increase the temperature so the model explores more varied styles

stem: An assistant must answer questions using both a product database and policy documents. Which design fits best?

choices.text: Let the assistant query the database for facts and retrieve policy passages, then combine both in its answer
Use only the database and ignore the policy documents to keep the design simple
Ask the model to recall database values and policies from its general training data
Put the entire product database and all of the policy documents into every single prompt for completeness

stem: Which TWO factors most affect whether a model trained last year still performs well today? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Whether the company changed its office furniture during the past year
Whether employees renamed the folder where the model's reports are saved
Whether the patterns in the real-world data have changed since training
Whether the company's website uses a new color scheme for its homepage
Whether the population the model serves has shifted in important ways

stem: A company wants to reduce customer wait times. Option 1 is an AI chatbot; option 2 is fixing a confusing checkout page that causes most support calls. Which reasoning is sound?

choices.text: Do both at the same time without assessing which one addresses the underlying cause
Fix the root cause first, since removing the source of calls may deliver more value than automating answers
Always choose the AI chatbot, since AI solutions are more modern and impressive than fixing existing web pages
Do neither, since customer wait times cannot be improved by technology changes

stem: A company sets an AI vision of 'augmenting every employee.' Which step makes this vision actionable?

choices.text: Buy an AI license for every employee in the company and consider the vision achieved immediately
Repeat the vision statement in every company meeting without further planning
Wait for employees to find their own uses without any guidance or measurement
Identify priority roles and tasks where AI assistance creates the most value, with targets

stem: A company introduced AI to answer HR questions. Which measure best reflects employee experience value?

choices.text: The length of each answer produced by the assistant in words
Time to resolve HR questions and employee satisfaction with the answers
The number of times the assistant's name was mentioned in emails
The number of HR policies stored in the AI assistant's knowledge base

stem: A company worries a competitor will copy its AI-powered feature within months. Which strategy best sustains its lead?

choices.text: Keep improving the feature with proprietary data and customer feedback faster than competitors can
Hide the feature from customers so competitors do not learn it exists
Lower prices on all products across the catalog to discourage competitors from building the same feature
Patent the idea of using AI for the feature and stop investing in improvements

stem: Which TWO practices improve the credibility of AI value reporting to executives? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Change the success metrics each quarter to match whatever improved
Replace measured results with projections whenever results disappoint
Report only the best-performing week of results each quarter
Report results against the baseline and targets agreed before launch
Include costs and negative side effects, not only benefits

stem: A company wants to use AI to enter a new market segment. Which TWO factors most determine whether AI creates a real advantage there? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of AI press releases the company has published
The number of AI conferences its executives attend each year
Ability to integrate AI into the segment's customer workflows
The size of the company's headquarters building
Access to data about that segment that competitors lack

stem: A company can invest in one large AI transformation program or in a sequence of smaller initiatives. It has limited AI experience. Which approach is usually wiser?

choices.text: One large program immediately, since big investments always produce bigger returns
A sequence of smaller initiatives that build capability and evidence before larger bets
Invest in whichever option the lowest-cost vendor happens to recommend during its sales process
No investment until AI technology stops changing, to avoid choosing the wrong tools
